The Prime Minister's Principal Secretary, P.K. Mishra, addressing the MoSPI Conclave at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: ANI
Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister P.K. Mishra has called for seamless coordination across government departments and a stronger focus on citizen experience, rather than the merely number of programmes administered, at a ‘National Workshop’ on ‘Leadership as Mission’.
Mr. Mishra was delivering the keynote address at an event organised by Niti Aayog to draw on the learnings from 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi as ‘Head of Government’.
The workshop was the first in a series of five such events announced by Niti Aayog to mark Mr. Modi assuming office as Chief Minister of Gujarat in October 2001.
Mr. Mishra said India’s governance journey has been marked by defining milestones that demonstrate the power of decisive leadership and the ability to translate vision into action.
“From the swift response to the 2001 Kutch earthquake to the country’s coordinated response to the COVID-19 pandemic, from expanding India’s footprint in the global space economy to the transformative impact of the Lakhpati Didi initiative, these actions reflect how strong political will, a responsive administration and mission-driven governance can bring about meaningful change in people’s lives,” Mr. Mishra said.
In his remarks, NITI Aayog Vice Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri said strong political and administrative leadership is crucial in driving India’s development journey.
“The transformational vision of our Prime Minister marks a significant shift in India’s national aspiration to become Viksit by 2047, reflecting the country’s transition towards a developed, prosperous and globally competitive nation,” he said.
Niti Aayog member R. Balasubramaniam, explaining the design and structure of the workshop, said the proceedings were structured to move from experience to analysis and from analysis to practice.
